playbook:
When prompted for hide, pick a cell by randomizing within a chosen zone each round (rotate among center, off-center, and edge) so I do not repeat the same number more than twice in a row.

When asked for a public station note, post a neutral, short status line (e.g., "steady on station" or "Diagnostics nominal") rather than actionable instructions or promises.

When my standing order names a target, follow the order and name that target unless I have a specific reason to deviate (Harbor present and firing on Harbor would trigger the severe penalty — do not target Harbor).

When I must pick a firing cell against a target, vary my probe pattern: do not always fire the same number. Cycle through a small set of cells (e.g., three different cells) across consecutive rounds to probe their hiding pattern rather than repeating one cell each round.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, always file the claim that matches the true result without deviation.

When choosing an escort claim, only claim an escort if I have a reasonable signal that the other boat will reciprocate (if notes or prior behavior indicate cooperation). Otherwise file [salvage: none]; random or unilateral escort claims are wasted points.

When I want mutual escort points, use my public note to signal intent (short, clear reciprocal phrasing) only if I judge the other boat likely to reciprocate; do not rely on uncoordinated salvage claims.

When Harbor explicitly warned about firing on it, treat that as absolute: do not target Harbor under any circumstances.

When my shot hits, consider repeating a proximate cell in the next round to exploit potential target predictability, but only if the target’s prior behavior suggests they stay; otherwise move my probing pattern.

When my shots are repeatedly missing and not yielding information, shift to a different probe set rather than persisting with the same cells — repeating the same unsuccessful cell pattern did not work.

When score tradeoffs arise, prefer reliable mutual escort points over low-probability speculative hits unless I have strong evidence of a hit location.

When writing short reasoning for the move (if a line is allowed), keep it one brief sentence focused on tactic, no extra commentary.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a central cell (4–6) on the first round to be unpredictable, then move at least two cells from my previous hide if I was reported hit last round.

When asked to hide and I was not hit last round, I vary my hide by 1–2 cells from my previous position to avoid a simple oscillation pattern.

When posting a note, I keep it bland and consistent with formation language (e.g., "steady on station" or "holding station") unless I want to signal a real coordination opportunity; do not give misleading positional information.

When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I fire at that named boat unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (Harbor present and vulnerable, or I have scored a confirmed hit and can finish them).

When choosing a fire cell against the assigned target, alternate between a central-concentrated search (4–6) in early rounds and wider sweeps (1–3 or 7–9) later; if a previous shot at the same target was a hit, follow up by shifting ±1 cell to try to secure a finish.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always report it truthfully ([claim: hit] or [claim: miss]) because claims must match the private report.

When Harbor is a valid target, do not fire on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty and the tactical payoff; otherwise avoid firing on Harbor.

When deciding an escort claim, claim an escort only if I reasonably expect reciprocity (e.g., mutual notes or prior non-hostile interaction) — otherwise claim none. Do not routinely claim escorts without basis.

When I receive repeated misses from a particular shooter against me, assume they are not focusing on my current cell; when I see a shooter repeatedly miss another target, expect them to change pattern and adjust hiding accordingly.

When the opportunity for mutual escort arises (both names can plausibly be offered), opt in to try to secure +5 each; otherwise preserve credibility by claiming none.

When given the choice between conserving ammo and attempting a risky finish on a target, prefer finishing a target if the hit would net me more points than the cost/risk; otherwise conserve and search.

When forced to choose a single rule in ambiguous situations, follow the standing-order firing sequence and truthful claims as primary constraints.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell by a simple pseudo-random rule (e.g., (previous hide + 3) mod 9, mapped to 1–9) so my pattern is unpredictable but reproducible for me; never pick the same cell twice in a row.

When asked for a station note, I post a neutral, non-informative phrase (e.g., "steady on station") unless I have a coordinated plan with another player to convey meaning.

When the standing order tells me whom to shoot, I fire at that named station unless there is a compelling strategic reason not to (see Harbor rule). Pick a number that follows my hide-randomization rule when I have no additional intel; if I have a confirmed hit location on that target from my own prior shot, bias the chosen cell toward that hit (repeat the hit cell with modest probability).

When the office privately tells me whether my shot was a hit or miss, I always file the matching public claim. Never lie about the private result.

When considering a shot at Harbor, do not fire at Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed 3-point transfer to the shooter and being put off the board is an acceptable tradeoff for my objectives. In practice, avoid firing on Harbor.

When making an escort claim, name the other boat only if I have a clear, reciprocal agreement (both of us will name each other) to secure the 5-point payout; otherwise file "none." Never name a boat that does not exist or that I have no reasonable chance of reciprocity with.

When I get a confirmed hit on a boat, prioritize continuing pressure on that boat in subsequent opportunities (reuse the hit cell with higher probability) because confirmed information is actionable; however, maintain diversity so opponents cannot easily predict my exact repeat.

When I observe others consistently targeting the same predictable players, I shift my hide pattern away from their inferred focal cells to reduce my chance of being hit.

When the game asks for any claim or name, validate that input against allowed values (1–9 for coordinates, actual live boat names for escorts/targets) before submitting.

When I have no alliance communication, default to conservative play: neutral notes, no escort, follow standing order for firing, truthful claims, randomized hides.
